title.title: Ball, tube, slab: the isoperimetric profile of the cubic 3-torus
title.subtitle: Claim: least-area regions in $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ are balls, then round tubes, then slabs, as the volume grows

plain: In a cube world that wraps around like a video game, the cheapest wrap is a ball, then a tube, then a slab

beats.text: Three shapes compete: a ball, a tube around a shortest loop, a slab between two faces
The profile is the lowest of the three: $\min\{(36\pi)^{1/3}v^{2/3},\ 2\sqrt{\pi v},\ 2\}$
The switches happen at $4\pi/81$ and $1/\pi$, where both shapes minimize

steps: Any least-area region is a smooth surface of some genus
Reflection symmetry and curvature-area estimates rule out handles
Only ball, tube and slab remain: the lowest one wins

achievement.label: Ball–tube–slab conjecture (Hauswirth–Pérez–Romon–Ros, 2004)
achievement.context: Before: small volumes (Morgan–Johnson) and near half volume (Acerbi–Fusco–Morini) only
achievement.note: Higher-genus competitors are excluded by reflection symmetry

voice.text: In a cube whose faces wrap around, three shapes compete to enclose a volume cheaply.
Reflection symmetry and curvature area estimates rule out every shape with handles.
Claimed: ball, then tube, then slab.

sources.quote: In the unit cubic flat torus R^3/Z^3 the isoperimetric profile is min{(36 pi)^{1/3} v^{2/3}, 2 sqrt(pi v), 2} with v = min(V,1-V); minimizers are exactly balls (V <= 4 pi/81), round tubes about shortest geodesics (4 pi/81 <= V <= 1/pi), slabs (1/pi <= V <= 1/2) and complements, with both types at the transitions.
Ball-cylinder-slab conjecture stated by Hauswirth-Perez-Romon-Ros (2004) and Ros

Higher-genus competitors are excluded with reflection symmetry and curvature-area estimates. The full classification, equality cases included, is in Lean (`OAI/Geometry/CubicTorus`, about 141,000 lines)
I did not build the Lean library (no compilation allowed)
